architectural_units.name: Client
architectural_units.description: The client is the component that formulates service requests.

architectural_units.name: Server
architectural_units.description: The server is the component that receives, processes, and returns responses to the client.

architectural_units.name: Presentation Layer
architectural_units.description: The presentation layer receives requests and builds responses.

architectural_units.name: Business Logic Layer
architectural_units.description: The business logic layer applies the domain rules.

architectural_units.name: Data Access Layer
architectural_units.description: The data access layer interacts with the database.

architectural_units.name: Domain Layer
architectural_units.description: The domain layer defines the data model.

architectural_units.name: View
architectural_units.description: The View component is formed by the HTML and SCSS files of each component that make up the application.

architectural_units.name: ViewModel
architectural_units.description: The ViewModel component groups the TS files of the components and their associated services.

architectural_units.name: Model
architectural_units.description: The Models are the TypeScript classes that define the data contract consumed by the view and the ViewModel.

architectural_units.name: Leader Service
architectural_units.description: This microservice has the main function of routing all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.

architectural_units.name: Portal Service
architectural_units.description: The portal microservice has the main function of offering a centralized interface for access to the different VWGS applications.

architectural_units.name: Access Control Service
architectural_units.description: The Access Control microservice has as its main objective the management of user authentication and their permissions within the application.

architectural_units.name: Communication Log Service
architectural_units.description: The Communication Log microservice has as its main purpose to record all communications that occur within the system.

architectural_units.name: Scheduler Service
architectural_units.description: This microservice has as its main function the planning and programming of processes within the system.

architectural_units.name: Angular
architectural_units.description: Framework used for the frontEnd of the application.

architectural_units.name: Spring Boot
architectural_units.description: Framework used for the backEnd of the application.

architectural_units.name: HTTP
architectural_units.description: Protocol used for message exchange between client and server.

architectural_units.name: JSON
architectural_units.description: Data format used for message exchange.

architectural_units.name: Amazon Web Services
architectural_units.description: Cloud provider for the project.
The Leader microservice has as its main function the routing of all communications to the corresponding microservice within the system architecture.
The client formulates service requests, and the server receives, processes, and returns responses to the client.
The services are the ones responsible for orchestrating HTTP calls to the server.
The data access layer interacts with the database.

patterns.name: Microservices
patterns.description: The application has an architecture based on microservices, which consists of dividing the system into a set of small, independent, and autonomous services.

patterns.name: Cloud Architecture
patterns.description: The application is designed, deployed, and executed using cloud services instead of local or physical servers.

patterns.name: Client-Server
patterns.description: The application follows the Client-Server pattern which organizes the code into two differentiated components: the client and the server.

patterns.name: MVVM
patterns.description: Angular applies the MVVM (Model-View-ViewModel) pattern, as its architecture is based on components and services.

patterns.name: Layered Architecture
patterns.description: Spring Boot organizes the code following the layered pattern with which responsibilities are separated.
